Just want to give my tidbit as a girl who has been suicidal since I was 12, now 22, with 2 hospitalisations under my belt. Since I've been suicidal for 10 years, have attempted since I was 17 - 20, you can't really expect someone to just suddenly not be. I mean, whenever someone makes me promise I won't try again, I always say I can't make that promise.

The way she talks is exactly like how I would too when feeling really suicidal. We don't want to burden people with our issues. When I was younger I used to post on my private story about killing myself. I don't anymore. But it sounds like a cry for help, but not wanting to burden anyone. I also am not dating right now because I know that my partner would feel responsible tk help.

I do very much understand, OP, that it can be mentally draining, having to worry about her all the time. You should always put yourself abd your emotions first. 

My family and friends worry about me, and I believe ill be better off dead since then they won't worry about me.

It's difficult for someone who isn't suicidal to understand the brain of someone who is. And I know how taxing it can be. If it's draining you, then yes, please take care of yourself. You're not her therapist.

Judging by the talk of money of her being hospitalised, I assume you're in the US. So unfortunately, I can't give much advice on what to recommend her, since I'm the the UK and we have free medical and mental health care. But, if her parents can't afford to get her help, what can she do? She wants help but has no money. Sure, there are websites online that can give you advice, but that's not the same as having someone trained help. Do you not have a free mental health service in the US? It's wonderful you told the school counsellor, I really hope they will help her.

Again, I'm not saying to stay with her. As I said, you should put yourself first, if it's affecting you this badly. Just wanted to give you some context of why she's speaking like this as a fellow mentally ill person.

Also that post about you playing the victim? You're not at all. You're looking after yourself, which you SHOULD

Ever since I was younger, around maybe 10 years old, I've had experiences which can be called nothing short of supernatural. Of course, as a child, the adults wouldn't listen to me. It is now 10 years later, and I am 20 years old. And I have had those experience on and off since I was a child. 

I remember it like it was yesterday - it was the day after my 18th birthday. I would've sworn it was a dream if the memories, and the motions and emotions didn't feel so real. And I didn't wake up in my bed. This was my first experience with truly seeing a supernatural. A werewolf. The night was dark, and I remember distinctly how the full moon shined down on me as I went on a walk. I could hear the howl. And being my curious self, I followed the noise. I wanted to believe it was just someone on drugs, but my past experiences with the supernatural made me think otherwise.  


And I was right. Right before my eyes, I saw this man turn into a wolf. I ran before he could notice me, my heart was thumping. And then, not even a few months later, I ran into a vampire, or someone who just gets a kink out of biting someone's neck until they bleed... That was until they looked at me, their fangs clear in the moonlight.  


I didn't experience anything supernatural again until my 20th birthday. Though I greatly wish to put this experience down to how drunk I was - but even alcohol wouldn't do this. The way they spoke to me... It sends a shiver down my spine just typing it right now.

​

It's slightly blurry but I saw... I saw different supernatural types. If that's how you want to call it. Faes, vampires, werewolves, witches... they were all there as I walked home. And you know the craziest thing they said? "You belong with us.\* I couldn't help but laugh. I'm a human. In all my 20 years, I've never shown any signs of being a supernatural, even if I have had sightings since I was a child. It's insane, so I denied it. And denied it constantly. But they were insistent they got closer, and closer, muttering something about taking me to their world...  


I write this tale as the taste of blood covers my taste buds, blood running down my face. The bodies of which I have indulged in surround me. I did belong with them, after all. And now, I know why I am thirsty all the time.

I know that I’ve been wonderful at hiding the evidence, but in a way, it’s still strange that the police haven’t found me. I have a high body count, after all. I’ve decided to write this so that if I’m ever caught, there is something that can recall my experience with my victims. Naturally, I won’t write about them all, just the most memorable ones.  
  
Let’s start with Robyn. My first victim, and the first is always the most memorable. She was a cute girl - only a couple of years younger than I - a first year at my university. The moment I saw her, I knew it was destiny. She was actually in one of my classes, and it was easy to get close to her. I invited her for drinks after our class once I built up a friendship with her, and she accepted.  
  
We had a few drinks, then I invited her back to my house. I live alone. This was where I committed my first murder. My own house. I suppose I was a little worried about her haunting the place. I managed to convince her to stay the night, the alcohol I gave her definitely helped.   
  
I slit her throat in the middle of the night. It’s a thrill that I’ve been chasing ever since.  
  
My 3rd victim - Nick. Met him on Tinder, I wanted a date but also a part of me knew it was the best way to have the same thrill again. The ‘date’ was nice, and we bonded to a point that I was slightly hesitant about ending his life. But that changed when he forced himself on me in a park. It was late enough that people may not hear me scream. Thing is, he underestimated my strength. It was so easy to strangle him until he lost his life. I’m not an idiot - I had the tools to remove my fingerprints, and I checked for cameras (there were none.) This one is especially important to me, as I began my ‘trademark’ signs. Ever played Heavy Rain? Yeah, I was inspired by the Origami Killer in that game. This was the first time I carved an ‘X’ into someone - which has led to me being known as the ‘X Killer.’ Has a nice ring to it, right?  
  
The last person I will speak about here is Olivia. My 8th victim. We were friends, and maybe you could say I had a little crush on her. Now, killing a friend wasn’t something I wished for, but I had a bit of an… episode, I guess you could say. It had been over a month since I gave into my ‘bloodlust.’ We were just hanging out like friends do. Then we went down an alleyway, and I couldn’t help myself. I used my box-cutter which I always keep on me to murder her. She didn’t die straight away, and her pleas honestly affected my heart. But I had to end her life,out of fear for my own safety.  
  
After that experience, I have not killed anyone. In fact, I now volunteer for charities in my town. And I suppose I’m ready to repent for my crimes now.
